title: Melody
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 2 Creative Activities; not yet checked by a CBC Creative Activities teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Use short tunes the class knows. Draw the shapes on the board as the song is sung.

skills.key_step: The child says if two tunes are the same or different and shows a song with shapes: the same shape for a tune that returns.
steps: Listen to the next tune: same or different?
Same: same shape. Different: new shape.
contexts: a game song in the field

board.do: Sing line 1 and draw a circle.
Line 2 is the same tune. Which shape?

misconceptions.ask: Two lines have the same tune but different words. Are the tunes the same?
The first tune comes back again. Which shape do you draw?
misconceptions.repair: Sing the song and point to the shape each time the first tune returns.

misconceptions.ask: The same tune is sung louder. Is it a different tune?
misconceptions.repair: Sing it softly and loudly; ask if the notes moved.

misconceptions.ask: In our song we drew a circle, a triangle, then a circle. What does the second circle show?
misconceptions.repair: Say: the shape only tells same or different.

checks.question: Same tune, new words: same or different tune?
Which shape do you draw when a tune comes back?

skills.key_step: The child keeps a known tune and fits new words to it, one word part for each note, so the words make sense.

floor.prerequisite: Knows when a tune is the same.
floor.question: Hum this tune. Is it the same as before?

steps: Pick one idea for the words.
Fit one word part to each note.

board.do: Clap the four notes of the line.

misconceptions.ask: You put new words to a song you know. What happens to the tune?
misconceptions.repair: Sing the old words, then the new words, while humming partners keep the tune.

misconceptions.ask: The line has four notes. How many word parts fit?
misconceptions.repair: Clap the notes, then clap the new words, and compare.

misconceptions.ask: Do the new words of a song need to make sense?
misconceptions.repair: Sing a nonsense line and a sensible one; ask which tells us something.

misconceptions.ask: Can you sing new words about washing hands to a tune you already know?
misconceptions.repair: Sing a hand-washing verse to a tune the class knows.

checks.question: When you put new words to a tune, does the tune change?
How many word parts go on each note?
